findings.problem: The trick says Germans use cool only for awesome, but it also commonly means calm or laid-back, as in bleib cool.
findings.fix: trick: COOL is borrowed straight from English and sounds the same; Germans use it for awesome or laid-back, but never for chilly.

back.example: Your new bike is really cool.

note: The prompt alone would almost always get cool, but the hint usefully rules out kühl.
